\section{Program adherence and prior-work recovery}
\label{sec:program-adherence}

This package follows the Citlali Scientific Contract Library Program, its
pilot process controls, and the owner-approved downstream sequence recorded by
the sanitized Scope Brief.  It begins after the frozen SCI-MAP scientific
authority without altering it.  The author received only the exact approved
SCI-JINC packet, the exact external objects admitted through packet covers,
the exact targeted r0.2 repair directive, the exact final targeted r0.3
owner-review directive, the final freeze-preflight directive, and the owner's
two explicit statements bound by
\texttt{SCI-JINC-DEC-PHASE-CENTER-001}.
No implementation, configuration, test, audit, repair, validation, reduction,
status, production, or manager-side record supplied normative scientific
content.  Non-packet records were restricted to process and exact-byte
closure.  The superseding freeze manifest binds the complete final authority
set and preserves each source's admitted role.

Prior work is reused rather than repeated.  The recovered signed estimator
with distinct numerator, signed normalization, and quadratic accumulator is
adopted.  The generic OTF/JINC analytic family is cited through the admitted
Schloerb method excerpt \cite{schloerb2019}.  The earlier circular radial-cutoff
and pixel-area-average branches are superseded by the approved fully populated
square cache and point-phase operator.  Response and covariance mathematics is
preserved conditionally for future science, but no such base-v0.1 product is
created.  Historical implementation behavior, parameter recommendations,
audits, and achieved results remain excluded.

The genuinely new Stage B work is therefore documentary and contractual: one
shared scientific authority is expressed as this rationale and the companion
Engineering Conformance Specification.  The shared modules define notation,
definitions, equations, assumptions, requirements, and falsifiable
predictions.  No estimator re-derivation is performed merely to make the work
appear new.

The exact source closure used by both views is reported in
Appendix~\ref{app:source-closure}.  The superseding freeze manifest binds the
sixteen original admitted objects, later owner directives and decisions, and
the final frozen authority and verification artifacts.  It preserves each
source's exact role and does not enlarge any source beyond its admitted use.

\section{Physical model and scientific intent}
\label{sec:physical-model}

An on-the-fly observation samples the sky irregularly.  The telescope and
upstream processing determine which spatial information is present in those
samples; gridding then estimates values on a regular destination WCS.  The
generic JINC motivation is spatial-frequency control: the peak-normalized
Fourier partner of a circular aperture passband is a signed JINC function
\cite{schloerb2019}.  A practical analytic family multiplies one JINC factor by
a generalized-exponential envelope and a second JINC factor.  The second
factor places a controlled zero while the envelope damps distant sidelobes.

The scientific object is not a nearest-neighbor average and not an ordinary
positive interpolation kernel.  Positive lobes, analytic zeros, and negative
lobes are all part of the operator.  The sign carries physical mathematical
meaning: a negative lobe subtracts from both the signal numerator and the
normalization, while it enters the quadratic statistic and coefficient-squared
time through its square.  Removing that sign would change the estimator.

The generic analytic identity is completely specified by
Equations~\eqref{eq:peak-jinc} and \eqref{eq:analytic-kernel}.  The angular
separation is normalized by an explicit array-associated scale $s_a$.  The
dimensionless tuple $(a_a,b_a,c_a,(r_{\max})_a)$ controls the two JINC
arguments and envelope.  This defines what each parameter means; it does not
select TolTEC values.  The Schloerb excerpt supplies a generic LMT method, not
TolTEC array tuning, validation, or performance authority.

\section{Scientific boundary and ownership}
\label{sec:ownership-narrative}

SCI-JINC begins with one exact PTC occurrence and the AST continuous
coordinate for the same processed sample realization.  PTC owns the
transformed quantity, retention, cleaning realization, immutable lineage, and
the one versioned registry of positive analysis/gridding coefficient families.
Every family declares permission for named consumers; permission for SCI-MAP
does not imply permission for SCI-JINC.  The accepted request selects one
explicitly permitted family, or one exact owner-authorized versioned mode
policy selects it.  No ambient or implementation default is authorized.
Requested, effective, observation-resolved, and realized identities remain
distinct.

AST owns the coordinate, frame, WCS, parent-sample association, validity,
uncertainty, and producer causes.  SCI-JINC does not reconstruct pointing or
infer a coordinate from row order, time tolerance, detector order, shape, or
numerical equality.  It consumes the AST coordinate only after the exact
same-processed-sample relation is established.

SCI-JINC owns JINC upstream-occurrence admission (Registry identity
\path{SCI-JINC:jinc_map_contribution@1}), local offset and radial
geometry, center rounding, point phase, square membership, signed coefficient,
normalization, cancellation conditioning, fixed accumulators, local map
support, grouping, destination identity, and atomic publication.  It applies
upstream facts without changing their meanings.  A producer cause has an
effect only when an exact restriction names it; generic flags do not acquire a
universal downstream veto.

This division follows the producer--transformer--consumer rule.  ALIGN/AST,
RTC, CAL, PTC, and VAL retain their own meanings.  Later noise, filtering,
beam, source, observing-mode, and recurrence packages retain theirs.  SCI-JINC
does not create those sciences at the gridding boundary.

\section{Analytic kernel, point phase, and finite geometry}
\label{sec:geometry-narrative}

The target is a finite rectangular FITS pixel grid
$\mathcal D=\{1,\ldots,N_x\}\mathbin{\times}\{1,\ldots,N_y\}$ with integer pixel
centres.  The exact AST coordinate for occurrence $i$ is
$\boldsymbol{u}_i=(x_i,y_i)$ in those same one-based
continuous pixel coordinates.  Centre resolution is componentwise:
\[
 c_{i\mu}=\left\lfloor u_{i\mu}+\tfrac12\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 \phi_{i\mu}=u_{i\mu}-c_{i\mu}\in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12),
 \qquad \mu\in\{1,2\}.
\]
An exact half-pixel tie therefore selects the larger integer and has residual
phase $-1/2$.  The scientific owner retains this positive-axis directional
tie as an intended part of the discrete operator.  The resolved WCS axis
order and signs are normative: reflecting
or reindexing an axis creates a different target-WCS identity rather than an
alternative interpretation of this tie rule.

Let $n_{\mathrm{sub}}=\texttt{subpixel\_n}$ be any exact positive integer selected by
the accepted request or by one exact owner-authorized versioned mode policy.
Each axis is partitioned into equal left-closed, right-open bins.  The logical
bin and its midpoint representative are
\[
 q_{i\mu}=\left\lfloor n_{\mathrm{sub}}
      (\phi_{i\mu}+\tfrac12)\right\rfloor,
 \qquad
 \widehat\phi_{i\mu}=-\tfrac12+
      \frac{q_{i\mu}+\tfrac12}{n_{\mathrm{sub}}}.
\]
Thus $q_{i\mu}\in\{0,\ldots,n_{\mathrm{sub}}-1\}$, and a phase exactly on an interior
bin boundary selects the upper bin.  No parity restriction is imposed.  In
particular, an even $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ maps $\phi=0$ to the representative
$+1/(2n_{\mathrm{sub}})$; that result is disclosed and normative, not repaired by a
hidden special case.  Under \texttt{SCI-JINC-DEC-PHASE-CENTER-001}, the
upper-bin convention and every positive integer $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ are
retained, including this one-sided exact-boundary phase offset.  The
mathematical cache key is the pair of bin indices
and the two integer offsets.  Physical cache layout is an engineering choice
only when it preserves that exact logical mapping.

The target WCS binds its celestial frame and topology, projection, reference
values, one-based reference pixel, dimensions, units, ordered axes, signs,
rotation, handedness, version, and a constant nonsingular $2\times2$ pixel
matrix $\mathbf M$.  Base v0.1 accepts only square, equal-scale, orthogonal
pixels:
\[
 \mathbf M^{\mathsf T}\mathbf M=\Delta^2\mathbf I,
 \qquad \Delta>0.
\]
Equivalently, $\mathbf M=\Delta\mathbf R$ with
$\mathbf R\in O(2)$; either handedness is permitted and recorded.  The
contractual angular separation is the Euclidean norm in this exact tangent
plane.  A skewed or anisotropic target WCS is typed incompatible; a scalar
pixel size may not conceal it.  This restriction narrows which AST-owned WCS
realizations JINC accepts and does not alter AST authority.

For array $a$,
\[
 h_a=\left\lceil\frac{s_a(r_{\max})_a}{\Delta}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol d\in\{-h_a,\ldots,+h_a\}^2.
\]
The destination pixel centre is
$\boldsymbol p=\boldsymbol c_i+\boldsymbol d$.  The exact normative discrete
point-phase radius is
\[
 \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol d}
   =\left\lVert\mathbf M
      (\boldsymbol d-\widehat{\boldsymbol\phi}_i)\right\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 \widehat r'_{i\boldsymbol d}=\widehat r_{i\boldsymbol d}/s_a,
\]
and Equation~\eqref{eq:analytic-kernel} is evaluated at that radius.  The
unquantized continuous phase is not a hidden reference oracle; the midpoint-
quantized operator above is the scientific operator.  Its exact-real-arithmetic
evaluation is the oracle for a later numerical certificate.

The disposition is directly observable at an exact integer pixel center.
For even $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, zero phase on both axes has representative
$(1/(2n_{\mathrm{sub}}),1/(2n_{\mathrm{sub}}))$.  At the nominal central
offset $\boldsymbol d=\boldsymbol0$, square-pixel orthogonality gives
\[
 \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol0}=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}n_{\mathrm{sub}}},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{i,\boldsymbol c_i}=\kappa_a\!\left(
 \frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}n_{\mathrm{sub}}s_a};
 a_a,b_a,c_a,(r_{\max})_a\right).
\]
This is the intended discrete scientific operator.  The nominal central
cache element is not replaced by the zero-radius limit $\kappa_a(0)=1$.

The exact constant in the second JINC factor is
$j_{1,1}=\min\{x>0:J_1(x)=0\}$.  A rounded decimal is at most nonnormative
guidance for an evaluator.  This definition makes the second factor exactly
zero at $r'=(r_{\max})_a$ while leaving analytic continuation beyond that
radius intact.

The square window is fully populated.  The half-width formula is a square
truncation rule, not a circular support predicate: outer rows and corners can
lie beyond $s_a(r_{\max})_a$ and are still evaluated.  Geometry first requires
$\boldsymbol c_i\in\mathcal D$.  If it fails, the occurrence contributes nowhere.
If it passes, a square member is retained exactly when
$\boldsymbol p\in\mathcal D$.  There is no radial cutoff, wrap, reflection,
completion, edge correction, or edge renormalization.  Direct construction on
a smaller map therefore need not equal larger-map construction followed by a
crop.

\section{Signed estimator and cancellation}
\label{sec:estimator-narrative}

The upstream $\omega_i$ is positive.  SCI-JINC supplies the signed spatial
factor $\kappa_{ip}$ and forms $w_{ip}=\omega_i\kappa_{ip}$.  For every
destination pixel it accumulates distinct $N_p$, $C_p$, and $Q_p$ using the
same occurrence membership and coefficient realization.  The normalized
estimate is $m_p=N_p/C_p$, not $N_p/Q_p$.  This choice gives unit response to a
constant input wherever the signed normalization is accepted.

Signed cancellation is the central validity issue.  A finite negative $C_p$
is scientifically admissible.  Exact $C_p=0$ is unavailable, not zero sky.
The dimensionless statistic $\rho_p=|C_p|/D_p$ describes the degree of
cancellation without introducing a unit-bearing threshold.  It is an
indicator, not a universal cutoff.

Algebraic support and numerical-realization adequacy are distinct.  Algebraic
support requires finite inputs and exact discrete coefficients, $Q_p>0$, and
$C_p\ne0$.  Numerical adequacy additionally requires one exact
owner-approved, versioned profile and one matching certificate bound to the
realization.  A profile must identify its scientific observable, absolute or
relative error form, reference magnitude or norm, complete parameter/source/
pixel domain, numerator and denominator treatment, near-zero behavior,
simultaneous or worst-case aggregation, exact inequality, certification
method, and lifecycle/provenance.  The certificate must identify the exact
discrete oracle, realization, source bytes, WCS, coefficient and parameter
states, and prove that the profile's inequality passes on its declared domain.

For a certificate that bounds denominator error by
$|\widehat C_p-C_p|\le\epsilon_{C,p}$, numerical support requires the exact
separation condition $|\widehat C_p|>\epsilon_{C,p}$.  If it does not hold,
zero remains inside the certified denominator interval and the normalized
value is unavailable.  Any additional normalized-map error inequality comes
from the exact profile; this contract does not invent one.  A profile without
a matching certificate, or a certificate without its exact profile, cannot
establish adequacy.

A passing $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NA}}$/$\mathcal E_p$ pair has a deliberately
narrow claim boundary: it establishes only finite-precision fidelity to the
exact selected discrete SCI-JINC oracle over the declared domain.  It does
not establish scientific adequacy of $s_a$, $a_a$, $b_a$, $c_a$,
$(r_{\max})_a$, $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, or square truncation; source-response or
beam fidelity; photometric or astrometric performance; optimality;
observational validation; response/covariance fidelity; readiness; or
production authority.  Qualifying a TolTEC parameter set remains a separate
scientific and observational program with its own objective, evidence,
authority, and lifecycle.

No exact owner-approved numerical-adequacy profile or matching certificate is
admitted or supplied by this source packet.  Numerical-adequacy state, and in
particular numerical near-cancellation support, is therefore typed
unavailable in this authority.  No qualitative instrument-fidelity phrase,
universal $\rho_p$ cutoff, unit-bearing floor, contributor-count/machine-epsilon rule,
summation algorithm, reduction order, or bitwise requirement substitutes for
that absent authority.

\section{Products, grouping, and lifecycle}
\label{sec:products-narrative}

Every produced bundle has exactly five required roles.  Three are primary
accumulator planes: $N_p$, $C_p$, and $Q_p$.  The fourth is derived $m_p$ with
its local support/validity state.  The fifth is
$T_p^{(\kappa^2)}$, the
\texttt{jinc\_coefficient\_squared\_time} coefficient-squared
temporal-accounting product.  It accounts for the squared analytic
coefficient divided by processed-sample frequency.  It
is not acquired exposure, complete temporal support, precision, validity, or
significance.

A whole-product failure in any required role suppresses the bundle.  A local
invalid pixel does not: local support is ordinary map content.  The fixed
schema therefore needs neither a generic role-availability object nor a
placeholder product.  It also creates no response, covariance, formal-weight,
physical-exposure, diagnostic, or generalized provenance role.

\subsection{Compact replayable generative record}
\label{sec:replay-record}

Reproducibility does not require dense per-contribution provenance or a sixth
numerical plane.  It does require one compact generative record at the
existing plan/bundle provenance granularity.  That record binds the exact
contract and source manifest; requested, effective, observation-resolved, and
realized identities; observation and occurrence-population rule; PTC and AST
parents; immutable admission-profile decision; coefficient family,
generation, payload and permission; parameter set; target WCS and metric;
rounding, tie, phase-bin and midpoint rules; square extent and edge membership;
destination; accumulator and cancellation rules; numerical profile and
certificate state; required-role completion/failure; lifecycle generation;
and the fixed ODQ-107 scope identity under which no response/covariance
companion information-state record exists.

Replay reconstructs the exact candidate occurrence population from the bound
parents, reapplies the immutable upstream-admission decision, resolves the
same centre, phase bin, representative, square, and cropped destination
membership, evaluates the exact discrete kernel, and then forms the coupled
accumulators in the declared numerical realization.  The record must make a
changed source, plan, coefficient, parameter, WCS, phase count, profile, or
generation distinguishable rather than treating it as the same result.  This
is compact generative lineage, not an authorization for a new generalized
provenance product or a per-pixel contribution archive.

\section{Validity, uncertainty, and claim separation}
\label{sec:validity-narrative}

Algebraic local support requires finite admitted inputs, finite $N_p$, $C_p$,
and $Q_p$, $Q_p>0$, and $C_p\ne0$.  Certified numerical-realization adequacy
is a separate state and is typed unavailable without the exact profile and
certificate.  Empirical downstream policy may narrow these states but cannot
promote an invalid pixel.  Outside square support, an analytic zero, and an
outside rounded center are ordinary no-contribution states.  Missing or
ambiguous coordinate association is different: geometry is unavailable and
must not be relabeled as outside support.

The formal variance and covariance equations are retained because they are
part of the recovered signed-estimator science.  They are conditional on the
exact coefficient family and covariance assumptions.  With dimensionless
$\omega_i$, $Q_p/C_p^2$ is dimensionless and is not signal variance.  Even
with inverse-square units, units alone do not prove inverse variance or
independence.  No formal-weight or covariance plane is therefore authorized
for the fixed bundle.

\section{Limiting cases and interpretive safeguards}
\label{sec:limiting-cases}

The signed estimator has simple limiting cases that expose its meaning without
requiring an implementation-specific realization.  For a constant field,
$z_i=z_0$ factors out of the numerator, so $N_p=z_0C_p$ and $m_p=z_0$ wherever
the normalization is accepted.  For one contributor with nonzero
$\kappa_{ip}$, the signed coefficient cancels between numerator and
normalization and the estimate returns that contributor's signal.  These are
normalization identities, not achieved photometric-validation claims.

Common positive scaling of every $\omega_i$ changes the three primary
accumulators together but leaves $m_p$, $\rho_p$, and the normalized operator
unchanged.  This distinguishes coefficient normalization from scientific
signal normalization.  A signal-unit change has its own transformation: when
an exact family truly represents inverse variance, scaling the signal by
$\lambda$ requires scaling the coefficient by $\lambda^{-2}$.  The map then
scales by $\lambda$ and the conditional formal weight by $\lambda^{-2}$.

                        >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.40\textwidth}
                        >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.26\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Interpretation of representative limiting cases.}\label{tab:limits}\\
\toprule
Case & Algebraic result & Scientific safeguard \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Case & Algebraic result & Scientific safeguard \\
\midrule
\endhead
Constant input & $N_p=z_0C_p$ and $m_p=z_0$ on accepted support. & Tests the
signed $N/C$ normalization, not achieved calibration. \\
One nonzero contributor & $m_p=z_i$ for either sign of $\kappa_{ip}$. & A
negative lobe is not an invalid sample. \\
Analytic zero & The occurrence changes none of $N_p$, $C_p$, $Q_p$, or
$T_p^{(\kappa^2)}$. & The zero remains distinguishable from outside support. \\
Finite negative lobe & $N_p$ and $C_p$ retain sign; $Q_p$ and time receive
positive squared terms. & Absolute value or clipping changes the operator. \\
Finite negative normalization & $m_p=N_p/C_p$ remains algebraically available
if every other gate passes. & Denominator sign alone is not a validity cut. \\
Exact cancellation & $C_p=0$ makes $m_p$ unavailable. & Never substitute zero
sky, infinity, or a valid non-finite value. \\
Near cancellation & Availability depends on the demonstrated total numerical
error under one exact owner-approved profile and matching certificate. & With
no admitted profile/certificate, numerical near-cancellation support is typed
unavailable; no universal $\rho_p$ threshold is inferred. \\
Outside rounded center & All $I_{ip}=0$, even with footprint overlap. & The
center-domain gate precedes square support. \\
In-map cropped edge & Retained pixels use their actual membership and signed
$N/C$ normalization. & No wrap, completion, edge correction, or
JINC-then-crop requirement. \\
Common coefficient scale & $N_p$, $C_p$, and $Q_p$ scale together; $m_p$ and
$\rho_p$ do not. & Coefficient normalization cannot silently change the map. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Coefficient-squared time has a different limiting structure.  Its term is
zero at an analytic zero and positive for either sign of a nonzero JINC lobe;
changing $\omega_i$ alone does not change it.  Those facts are exactly why the
product cannot be reinterpreted as weighted exposure, precision, or normalized
influence.

The edge rules deliberately make finite-map construction part of the
observation estimator.  An occurrence with an outside rounded center is
excluded before footprint evaluation, while an occurrence with an inside
center uses a cropped square.  Therefore a larger-map JINC construction
followed by cropping is not required to equal direct construction on a smaller
map.  This is a scientific boundary decision, not a numerical defect.

\section{Future evidence route without a validation claim}
\label{sec:future-evidence}

The companion engineering view converts the shared requirements and
predictions into an evidence checklist, but no evidence is evaluated during
Stage B authorship.  A future assessment must first bind the exact coefficient
family, TolTEC parameter set, observation, array, WCS, plan, destination, and
lifecycle generation.  Without those identities, a numerical example cannot
stand in for the scientific route.

Algebraic checks should begin with hand-constructed constant, one-contributor,
two-contributor, analytic-zero, negative-lobe, and cancellation cases.  Geometry
checks should then exercise every map edge and corner, half-pixel tie, phase-bin
edge, \texttt{subpixel\_n}$=1$, square-cache corner, and center immediately
inside and outside the finite domain.  These constructions establish the
operator being tested.  They shall use the exact half-tie, half-open-bin,
midpoint, WCS-metric, square-extent, and crop rules; there is no alternate tie
or bin algorithm within base v0.1.

Numerical adequacy requires the exact profile and certificate described in
Section~\ref{sec:estimator-narrative}.  The reference is exact-real evaluation
of the normative midpoint-quantized discrete operator.  Phase quantization is
therefore part of the operator, not realization error relative to an unlisted
continuous-phase target.  Analytic-function evaluation, cache/index
realization, finite arithmetic, accumulation/reduction, and normalized
division must be covered exactly as the profile declares.  Agreement between
two executions is useful evidence but is not itself the scientific criterion:
two paths could agree while sharing the same wrong membership or normalization.

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.23\textwidth}
                        >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.40\textwidth}
                        >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.27\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Future evidence layers and their present limits.}\label{tab:evidence-layers}\\
\toprule
Layer & Representative evidence & What it cannot establish alone \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Layer & Representative evidence & What it cannot establish alone \\
\midrule
\endhead
Authority binding & Exact parameter, coefficient, observation, WCS, plan,
destination, and lifecycle identities. & Numerical correctness or achieved
performance. \\
Algebra and units & Hand cases, scaling identities, zero limit, signed lobes,
and conditional unit classifications. & Implementation conformity without a
bound candidate. \\
Geometry and membership & Tie/bin neighborhoods, square corners, outside-center
gate, inside-edge crop, and exact AST association cases. & Observational
response or photometry. \\
Numerical adequacy & Exact owner-approved profile, matching certificate,
declared oracle/domain/error functional, and adversarial cancellation cases. &
Bitwise reproducibility, observational validity, or readiness. \\
Bundle/lifecycle & Array permutation, missing-array, destination collision,
chunking, atomic failure, and forbidden-role cases. & Representation fidelity
without stored-product evidence. \\
Representation & Exact stored identities, units, WCS, support state, and role
semantics. & Observational validation or production authorization. \\
Observation & Separately authorized response, covariance, photometric, and
science-performance evidence. & Readiness or production authority without an
explicit decision. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

A fail-closed test may demonstrate that missing parameter or coefficient
authority prevents a bundle.  It may not manufacture the missing authority in
order to exercise a numerical path.  Likewise, a future response or covariance
study must first receive separate product authority; base-v0.1 conditional
equations do not turn an observed output into an authorized companion product.

\section{Typed unavailability and next scientific dependencies}
\label{sec:typed-unavailability}

The contract defines the generic algebra and operator, but three authorities
needed for a numerically adequate route are not admitted or supplied by this
source packet.  First, an exact
PTC coefficient family must be registered, selected, realized, and explicitly
permitted for SCI-JINC.  Second, an exact TolTEC array-associated parameter set
must be scientifically authorized.  Third, one exact owner-approved
numerical-adequacy profile and a matching realization-bound certificate must
exist.  None of these absences is repaired by memory or software behavior.

No inherited 45~m denominator, inherited shape values, or mode-dependent
$r_{\max}$ values are authorized.  No value in the generic Schloerb excerpt is
a TolTEC default, recommendation, optimum, validation result, or performance
claim.  Selecting TolTEC parameters is a separate scientific exercise with a
named objective and appropriate TolTEC/LMT beam, response, and/or noise
evidence.

The targeted repair finds no unresolved Stage A scope discrepancy: the exact
ODQ-107 five-role amendment remains controlling.  A future proposal to replace
it with broader response, covariance, companion-availability, or provenance
information-state roles would require a bounded Stage A successor and renewed
exact-byte owner approval.  Physical exposure, cross-observation coaddition,
and broader diagnostics remain deferred until a concrete scientific use
separately authorizes them.
